newsitem.title: USA: New home sales in 1996 strongest in 18 years.
newsitem.headline: New home sales in 1996 strongest in 18 years.

text.p: Sales of new homes eased slightly in December after surging in November, the Commerce Department said Tuesday, and for the full year they posted the strongest gain in 18 years.

Sales fell 1 percent in December to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 783,000 units after a revised 17.7 percent jump in November. Sales for all of 1996 were up 13.3 percent from 1995 to 756,000 -- the strongest performance since 817,000 new homes were sold in 1978, the department said.
Previously, the department said sales in November had risen by 14.2 percent to a rate of 772,000.
December sales were significantly stronger than anticipated by Wall Street economists, who had forecast a rate of 745,000 sales for the month.
Analysts said more jobs and steady income gains, as well as a strong stock market throughout 1996, buoyed the housing market.

Mortgage rates have recently begun to creep upward, but in December the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. said rates for a 30-year mortgage averaged 7.60 percent, down from 7.62 percent in November. But it was higher than the 7.20 percent mortgage rate available a year earlier, in December 1995.

Sales in December were cushioned by a huge 46.7 percent increase in sales in the Midwest to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 176,000, the strongest sales pace since December 1993, when new homes were selling at a rate of 206,000 a year.
In all other regions, sales were down in December.
In the Northeast, sales fell 3.3 percent to a rate of 87,000 a year and in the South they decreased 6.7 percent to 335,000. Sales in the West were down 16.7 percent to 185,000 a year.

Sales of new homes peaked in 1996 at a rate of 820,000 a year in August and have declined in three of the four months since then for which figures have been released. Sales were down 5 percent in September and fell 13.7 percent in October before surging in November and then dropping again in December.
A similar trend is evident in sales of used, or existing homes.

Last week the National Association of Realtors said sales of existing homes fell 3.5 percent in December to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.87 million. But for all of 1996, sales rose 7.5 percent to a record 4.09 million, beating the previous record of 3.99 million homes sold in 1978.
The average home sales price in December fell to $173,200 from $174,200 in November, while the median sales price was down to $142,000 from $146,500.
